title: fix(metadata-protocol): deleting a runtime object hydrated at boot unregisters it at once; the metadata service's boot copy is not its code layer
body:
Fixes #23645

Clause-②: no

#23514 remains open. This PR is the delete-heal prerequisite that card's refusal needs. That card's prescription is "delete the package-less definition without `dropStorage`, then save naming the package", and after this PR it is a real in-process way out, with the table and records kept. This PR does not touch that card's branch or its refusal. The delete door's status and wording are unchanged.

## The defect, measured on `origin/main` `a647783d46`

The kernel was a real `ObjectKernel` with `MetadataPlugin` (a `NodeMetadataManager`, `watch: false`), `ObjectQLPlugin` with no `environmentId`, and a memory driver. A second kernel over the same store served as the boot. A runtime object was saved, given 2 records, and then hydrated at boot. `DELETE` with no package and no `dropStorage` answered `{ success: true, reset: true }` and "it no longer exists". The stored row was gone, but until the next boot:

- the registry owner stayed (`sys_metadata`, or the bound package);
- the data plane served the 2 records;
- `getMetaItem`, the object list and the layered read all served the deleted definition.

The same run repeated on the kernel's fallback metadata (no `MetadataPlugin`) gave the same result. Registry verbs spied for this object: `removeObjectOverlay -> false | removeRuntimeShadow -> false | registerItem(object)`, then a return. The same object saved and deleted in one process gave `... | removeOverlayEntry -> true | unregisterObject -> true`.

## The producer

`ObjectQLPlugin.start()` runs `bridgeObjectsToMetadataService` on a kernel with no `environmentId`. It copies every object the registry holds into the `metadata` service. That includes each runtime object hydrated from `sys_metadata`, whose copy carries the registry's `_provenance: 'org'` (measured: `{ _packageId: 'sys_metadata' or the bound package, _provenance: 'org' }`). Nothing removes the copy when the row is deleted. The protocol reads the `metadata` service as the CODE layer in four places, through one helper, `readItemFromMetadataService`:

- the heal's tier-2 baseline (`restoreArtifactRegistryView`);
- `getMetaItem` step 2;
- the layered `code` layer;
- the carry-forward's code layer.

The list merge reads the service through `metadataService.list`. So the heal re-registered the copy and returned before tier 3, and the reads served it too. An object saved in the same process was never copied, so its delete worked. A kernel with an `environmentId` never runs the bridge (the standalone stack defaults to `env_local`). Measured there, the same boot-hydrated delete was already correct.

## The fix, and its landing point

`readItemFromMetadataService` answers an `object` body stamped tenant-authored as a clean miss (not degraded). It uses the discriminator `getMetaItemLayered` already applies to the registry's plain key: the ADR-0010 marker read through `isTenantAuthored`, with no new marker. The list merge drops such `object` items from its base. The stored rows above that merge already serve every live object.

The heal's own code is unchanged. Only its tier-2 header gained a note. The walk now reaches tier 3, which unregisters the object, for a boot-hydrated runtime object as for one saved in the same process.

Why not the PM's suggested route alone (an `isArtifactBacked` predicate at tier 2): that route makes the registry and data plane agree. But measured with tier 3 reached and the copy left in the service, `getMetaItem` still served the deleted definition, the list still held it, and the layered `code` layer was still the copy. The card's "metadata read agrees" needs the read fixed too.

Two other landing points were rejected:

- **The bridge** (stop copying tenant-authored objects). MCP's stdio data bridge reads `metadataService.getObject` for `enforceApiExposure` (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`). Removing the copy would make that gate fall open to schema defaults for every boot-hydrated runtime object.
- **Retiring the copy from the heal** through `metadataService.unregister`. `MetadataManager.unregister` deletes through every writable `datasource:` loader, and `DatabaseLoader.delete` matches only `type` and `name`. On a host that wires one, that would delete an arbitrary `sys_metadata` row of the name, for example a draft.

**Scoped to `object`.** `plugin-security`'s security-catalog echo registers stored `permission` and `position` rows in the service on purpose, stamped `_provenance: 'org'` too. It keeps them current, and its pins read the layered `code` layer as the echo. Measured: with the predicate made type-agnostic, `security-catalog-echo.test.ts` went red (1 failed | 17 passed, `layered.code` read `null`). It is green with the `object` scope.

**File surface.** The claim named `restoreArtifactRegistryView`, its tier-2 baseline read included. That read is the shared helper above, so the change also reaches the three other code-layer readers of `object` bodies, all with the same defect class. The list merge (`readFlattenedMetaItems`) is outside the claimed surface. It is fixed in place under the bounded-fix exemption: same defect class, a mechanical one-predicate change, no other claim on that function, and the same gate family. Its pin and ablation leg are below.

## Hypotheses

- H1 confirmed, by the verb spy above.
- H2: the copy is not a code baseline. Confirmed, but the predicate that holds is the copy's own provenance at the shared read, not `isArtifactBacked` at tier 2 alone (see above).
- H3 confirmed. The service's copy is stale after the delete. Its producer is ObjectQL's boot bridge (`packages/objectql`), not `packages/metadata*`, and no delete propagates to it. The fix is at the protocol's code-layer read (reasons above).
- H4 measured. A runtime object bound to a real package has the identical defect (owner stayed `com.qa.p`, and a following save naming Q was refused `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` because P still owned it). The same fix closes it, pinned below.

## Pins

New file: `packages/objectql/src/protocol-delete-boot-hydrated-object-heal.test.ts`, on a real kernel with `MetadataPlugin`. Each case asserts the boot copy is present first, so a pass is never for an empty reason.

- For a package-less object and a package-bound one, after the delete:
  - the owner, `getObject`, `getMetaItem` (no item), the list, the layered read (`code`/`overlay`/`effective` all `null`) and the data plane (`OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` / `404`) agree the object is gone;
  - the table keeps its 2 records, and nothing is dropped.
- For both, a later save naming Q makes Q the owner. The data plane, the by-name read and the 2 kept records agree. After a 3rd insert, a boot agrees too (owner Q, 3 records).
- CONTROL: a code package's object (registered via `registerApp`, copied with `_provenance: 'package'`) reaching the same delete keeps its baseline. Tier 2 re-registers it, and it stays owned, served and dispatched.

## Negative control (a one-time ablation, not a permanent case)

`packages/objectql` reads `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` through `dist` (a `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS` pair), so every leg rebuilt and ran the preflight. The fix blob at HEAD is `5cde7e0e3ed8`.

- **Leg A**: deleted the read's guard (`ablation-replace`: anchor `1 -> 0`, blob `5cde7e0e3ed8 -> c175bc008d16`). Rebuild, then preflight `--absent`: marker absent from all 24 built files. Result: `Tests 4 failed | 1 passed`, each failing on the owner assertion. The CONTROL stayed green by design. Restore: blob back to `5cde7e0e3ed8` and `git diff HEAD` empty. Rebuild, then preflight present (1 built file, tree clean). Result: `Tests 5 passed`.
- **Leg B**: deleted the list filter (anchor `1 -> 0`, blob `5cde7e0e3ed8 -> f3d07653e65b`). Rebuild, then preflight `--absent`. Result: `Tests 4 failed | 1 passed`, failing on `not.toContain(NAME)` in the list. Restore proven the same way, then `Tests 5 passed`.

The predicted direction was red for both legs, and both were observed red.

## Local verification

All results below are on HEAD `b215fdeea`, which merges `origin/main` `c7dd48ab4` before opening (AGENTS.md §10). Every run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, and every one printed `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

- Build of the `@objectstack/objectql...` closure: exit 0.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` full suite (`vitest run --maxWorkers=2`): `Test Files 236 passed | 3 skipped (239)`, `Tests 20550 passed | 19 skipped`. Its `typecheck` exited 0.
- `@objectstack/objectql` full suite (`vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`): `Test Files 423 passed (423)`, `Tests 8123 passed (8123)`. Its `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck`) exited 0, with the test-layer debt unchanged at 39 files / 233 errors / 64 pinned signatures.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `src/security-catalog-echo.test.ts`, the control for the `object` scope: `Tests 18 passed`.
- New pin file: `Tests 5 passed (5)`.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `b215fdeea` derives 67 families.
  - 66 exited 0.
  - 1 is NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`. It reads every workspace package's `dist`, and only the `objectql` closure was built here. CI runs it in the required `Build Core` job.
  - `--ran` reconciliation: `67 derived, 66 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
  - Two gates first refused on the shallow clone: `check-engine-split-ratio.mjs --days 90` and `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`. Both exited 0 after `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-10 origin main`.

## Acceptance notes

- The `metadata` service's own boot copy stays stale on these kernels after a delete and after a save. Consumers of `IMetadataService` read it, for example MCP's stdio data bridge (`listObjects`, `describeObject`, and the `enforceApiExposure` gate, which reads `enable.apiEnabled` off it). This PR does not change that service. It is reported to the seat as a finding.
- Reach: the defect needs `ObjectQLPlugin` with no `environmentId`. That covers the CLI's host-config assembler (`new ObjectQLPlugin()`), `kernel-factory.ts` and a control plane. `createStandaloneStack` (default `env_local`) never had it, as measured.
- After a delete, `getMetaItem` answers its usual no-item envelope, and the REST door's 404 mapping is unchanged.
